At `state.now == Duration::ZERO` — the fake's default clock origin, since QueueState derives it — `defer(id, Duration::MAX)` gives `checked_add` = Some(Duration::MAX), whose as_secs() is u64::MAX and whose subsec_nanos() is 999_999_999, so the bare `+ 1` overflows and PANICS in a debug test binary instead of returning the Adapter error.<br><br>No current test hits it: `fake_queue_defer_overflow_refuses_without_poisoning_or_mutating` (contract_over_fakes.rs:424-442) calls `queue.advance(Duration::from_nanos(1))` first, which makes `checked_add` itself return None so the closure never runs. That test's expectation is spelled `.expect_err("overflow is an error, never a panic")` — the invariant is already written down, and the new code can violate it one `advance` call away.<br><br>SMALLEST FIX: mirror the store — `deadline.as_secs().checked_add(u64::from(...)).map(Duration::from_secs)` — so the overflow stays an error on both sides of the port, which is the whole point of the exercise.<br><br>AND IT IS RED RIGHT NOW. I ran it: `cargo test -p pij-testkit --test contract_over_fakes` -&gt; 18 passed, 3 FAILED — fake_queue_defer_pending_replaces_the_schedule_from_the_current_clock, fake_queue_defer_running_preserves_identity_body_attempt_and_delay, fake_queue_defer_zero_releases_pending_and_running_without_reordering_fifo. Sample: contract_over_fakes.rs:186 `left: not_before_ms: 1000, right: not_before_ms: 15`.<br><br>That is not an argument against the fix — it is the finding proving itself. Those three tests are the ones built on 10 ms and 30 ms delays, and they only ever passed because the fake was more precise than the store; the moment the fake tells the truth, assertions that could never have described SQLite fail. Expect to rewrite them in whole seconds (or assert the rounded deadline), and note that this is exactly the work `queue_contract` would have forced up front instead of discovering three assertions later. | crates/testkit/src/fakes.rs (uncommitted f3 remediation, defer rounding) vs crates/store/src/queue.rs:424-435 | — | — | — | — | — | — |
